title: Upgrade Impact Lens — network & cost scenario explorer
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Private cluster upgrades are high-risk for customers because an upgrade touches multiple dimensions simultaneously: kernel/runtime changes, model kernel selection, network paths (VPC routes, peering), and tenant egress/cost exposure. Operators need a compact, interactive view that explains the *impact* of a proposed upgrade across networking (latency/paths), estimated cost delta, and the safe rollback/actions available — all without leaving the upgrade flow.

Goal:
Design an "Upgrade Impact Lens" component embedded into the Private Console upgrade flow. The lens should: (1) simulate network and cost outcomes for the proposed upgrade, (2) surface tenants likely to be impacted with severity and expected latency delta, (3) offer guided rollback / canary-selection actions and one-click mitigations (traffic pinning, temporary downscaling, regional failover), and (4) be compact enough to appear inline with the upgrade summary and release notes.

Success metrics:
- Reduce manual pre-upgrade analysis time by ~50% for SREs and customer ops teams.
- Reduce upgrade rollbacks caused by avoidable network or cost regressions by 30% in the next quarter.
- Achieve an initial SUS usability score >= 75 in internal trials.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Lens appears inline on the upgrade confirmation page and can be expanded to full-screen.
2) Simulation runs within 6–12 seconds for typical cluster sizes (<= 50 nodes) using precomputed routing/cost profiles.
3) Display: per-tenant severity (low/medium/high), estimated p95 latency delta (ms), monthly cost delta (USD), and a suggested mitigation action.
4) Action buttons for: create canary cohort, pin traffic to previous model variant, schedule automatic rollback on threshold breach, and export CSV of impacted tenants.
5) UX handoff artifacts (Figma + spec) and an annotated accessibility checklist included.
6) Product sign-off and security review recorded in PRD before implementation.
discussion: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial draft of the lens concept and problem framing added. Emphasized network path visualization + per-tenant cost impact to make trade-offs visible to ops.

2026-03-11 Julian Ramos (Eng): Technical note — live path probing has significant N*P cost for large clusters; recommending hybrid approach: cached topology + targeted probes for changed routes. Will need an API endpoint: /v1/upgrade/simulate that returns tenant-level deltas.

2026-03-12 Arjun Patel: Noted dependency on backend epic ENG-32641 (upgrade-simulator-api). Added constraint: simulation must support 'what-if' toggles for model-quantization and node-type mix.
design_decisions: Hybrid simulation strategy: use cached routing + quick probes for changed links to meet response-time SLOs.
Compact inline card default collapsed to preserve upgrade flow; full-screen explorable panel for detailed per-tenant drilldown.
Severity bucket thresholds set to: low (<5ms p95 delta and <2% cost), medium (5–25ms or 2–10% cost), high (>25ms or >10% cost). These thresholds are configurable by cluster admins.
Expose mitigation actions directly in the lens (canary creation, traffic pin, schedule rollback) to shorten time-to-remediation.
All cost deltas include an audit line showing assumptions (billing period, egress vs compute split) and link to the cost model documentation.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Accuracy vs latency: Full live probing yields best accuracy but unacceptable runtime; hybrid approach trades some precision for performance.
Information overload: Showing every metric for large clusters could overwhelm operators — mitigated by prioritizing tenant severity and top-10 impact list.
Security posture: Simulation results expose tenant-level impacts; ensure results are available only to users with appropriate RBAC. Will require an auth check in the simulator API.
False confidence: Estimated impacts are probabilistic. Add prominent copy and 'assumptions' toggles to prevent over-reliance.
